pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, non-inferiority, multicenter study; isavuconazonium vs. voriconazole
pivotal_trials.endpoint: All-cause mortality through Day 42 (ITT population); 10% non-inferiority margin
pivotal_trials.result: All-cause mortality at Day 42: 18.6% (ISA) vs. 20.2% (VRC); treatment difference -1.0% (95% CI: -8.0%, 5.9%); non-inferiority demonstrated (upper bound 5.9% < 10% NIM). Day 84 mortality: 29.1% vs. 31.0%. Key secondary DRC overall response at EOT (mITT): 35.0% (ISA) vs. 36.4% (VRC).

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, multicenter, single-arm, non-comparative study; isavuconazonium monotherapy; historical controls and Fungiscope matched controls used for comparison
pivotal_trials.endpoint: All-cause crude mortality through Day 42 and Day 84; DRC-assessed overall response at EOT (secondary)
pivotal_trials.result: All-cause mortality at Day 42: 37.8% (95% CI: 22.5%, 55.2%); at Day 84: 43.2% (95% CI: 27.1%, 60.5%). Upper bound of 95% CI for ISA mortality (55.2%) is below lower bound for untreated historical controls (94.0%). DRC overall response rate at EOT: 31.4% (complete 14.3%, partial 17.1%).

advisory_committee.vote: 11-0 favorable for aspergillosis; 8-2 favorable for mucormycosis (Anti-Infective Drugs AC, Jan 22 2015)

key_safety: In the Phase 3 controlled trial (n=516), overall TEAEs occurred in 96.1% (ISA) vs. 98.5% (VRC) of patients; serious TEAEs in 52.1% vs. 57.5%; AEs leading to discontinuation in 14.4% vs. 22.8%; all-cause mortality 31.5% vs. 33.6%; hepatobiliary TEAEs in 8.9% vs. 16.2%; Hy's Law criteria met in 3 ISA vs. 7 VRC patients; QT shortening (not prolongation) observed with ISA; visual hallucinations reported less frequently with ISA (1.2%) vs. VRC (4.2%).
target_moa: Inhibition of fungal cytochrome P450-dependent lanosterol-14α-demethylase (sterol 14-alpha-demethylase), blocking ergosterol biosynthesis in fungi

_meta.indication:
CRESEMBA is an azole antifungal indicated for patients 18 years of age and older for the treatment of invasive aspergillosis.
CRESEMBA is an azole antifungal indicated for patients 18 years of age and older for the treatment of invasive mucormycosis.
Usage:
Specimens for fungal culture and other relevant laboratory studies (including histopathology) to isolate and identify causative organism(s) should be obtained prior to initiating antifungal therapy. Therapy may be instituted before the results of the cultures and other laboratory studies are known. However, once these results become available, antifungal therapy should be adjusted accordingly.

indication_details.population_restrictions: patients 18 years of age and older

supplements.description: Expanded the approved indications for Cresemba (isavuconazonium sulfate) to include pediatric patients: the injectable 372 mg formulation for patients "one year of age and older," and the capsule formulations (74.5 mg and 186 mg) for patients "six years of age and older who weigh 16 kilograms (kg) and greater," both for treatment of invasive aspergillosis and invasive mucormycosis.

advisory_committee_detail.vote: Q1 (invasive aspergillosis): Yes 11, No 0, Abstain 0; Q2 (invasive mucormycosis): Yes 8, No 2, Abstain 1
advisory_committee_detail.overall_recommendation: Favorable for both indications; broader support for aspergillosis (unanimous 11-0) than mucormycosis (8-2-1).

linkages.concern: Uncertainty around efficacy evidence for invasive mucormycosis given reliance on historical controls rather than a randomized controlled trial (2 'No' votes and 1 abstention on Q2)
linkages.change: Post-marketing commitment (PMC) established: registry to collect and analyze clinical efficacy-related outcome data on patients treated with isavuconazonium sulfate who have invasive mucormycosis or infection with non-fumigatus aspergillus species

linkages.concern: Potential for decreased susceptibility/resistance emerging in target organisms in the approved label population
linkages.change: PMR: conduct a prospective study over a five-year period to determine if decreased susceptibility to Cresemba is occurring in the target population of organisms in the approved label

linkages.concern: Long-term carcinogenic potential of isavuconazonium sulfate not fully characterized at time of approval
linkages.change: PMRs: conduct a two-year mouse carcinogenicity study and a two-year rat carcinogenicity study

linkages.concern: Labeling recommendations following affirmative votes on both indications (specific language not detailed in reviewed text)
linkages.change: Major safety concerns addressed in labeling; REMS determined not required; safety findings adequately addressed in product labeling per Division of Risk Management review

advisory_committee_detail.discussion_summary: The Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee reviewed isavuconazonium sulfate for two proposed indications: invasive aspergillosis and invasive mucormycosis. The committee voted unanimously (11-0) to support substantial evidence of safety and efficacy for invasive aspergillosis, and voted 8-2-1 in favor for invasive mucormycosis, reflecting some reservations about the single-arm historical control design used for the mucormycosis indication. The committee provided labeling recommendations following both affirmative votes.
